$comment: Everything written under the data directory, and what happens to each entry when that directory
moves. Read by BOTH halves' test suites, the way data-side-vectors.json already is.
WHY A FIXTURE RATHER THAN A LIST IN THE CODE. The list in dataDir.ts named four entries; the
server and the extension between them write more than twenty. Following the panel's own moving
instructions therefore lost a person's edited prompts, their whole spending history, the entire
chat half of the product and the committed rounds sitting in the write-ahead log - every one of
them silently, because a copy that misses a file reports success. A second hand-written list
would have drifted the same way the first one did, so the drift is what is tested: one suite
scans both halves' sources for paths composed under the data directory and fails on a path this
file has never heard of. A new persistent directory is then a red test on the day it is written.
THE THREE FATES.
move: true                 - carries history. It must be copied, or something is lost.
move: false, mention: true - must NOT be copied, and the panel says so by name, because both
wrong guesses are silent: worktrees/ moves somebody's checkout
onto a NAS for no benefit, and a token moved hands one machine's
sign-in to another - the thing the per-side layout exists to stop.
move: false, mention: false - written again by itself. Not worth a sentence on a panel.
PATHS ARE AS A PERSON READS THEM: a directory carries its trailing slash. The scan compares the
first segment, so 'consultations/' covers consultations/answers/ and consultations/locks/.
THE DATABASE'S TWO SIDECARS ARE NOT OPTIONAL. The journal mode is WAL, so committed transactions
live in coai.db-wal until a clean shutdown checkpoints them. A server that was killed leaves
rounds there, and a copy of coai.db alone loses exactly those - the newest ones - and reports
that it worked.
